info.description: REST API of the AI-HA framework, which backs up and restores workloads across clouds.
info.title: AI-HA REST API

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will take a node's measurements of its service and replication, and answer with its HA assignment. The system will come from the agent's token, never from the body.

Report the partitions that make up the calling agent's system, so that a backup can be asked for without naming them by hand. The report replaces any earlier one: a system keeps one inventory, and its layout history lives in the backup manifests. An agent that could not account for every filesystem the system needs says so, and backup targets are then not chosen automatically. The system is taken from the agent's token, never from the body.
post.summary: Report what this system is made of

get.description: Long-poll for work assigned to the calling agent's system. Returns the job as soon as one is waiting, or 204 when the wait elapses with nothing to do; the 204 is the normal idle path and must not be treated as an error or backed off. Receiving a job grants nothing: the agent must claim it and see the claim succeed before starting. Reaching this endpoint is also what marks the agent as alive.

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for work, clamped to 5-45
parameters.name: wait

post.description: Take a job handed out by the long poll. Work must not start until this succeeds: two agents can be handed the same job and only the claim decides between them. Retrying with the same request key before any progress is reported returns the same attempt with a new lease token, since the first response was evidently lost. The response carries the repository the job writes to, credentials included, decrypted for this response; if it cannot be opened the claim is not recorded and may be retried.

Report on a running attempt and renew its lease. Send this periodically whether or not the work advanced: it is what keeps the lease alive. A cancel request travels back on the response, as there is no other path to an agent.
Finish an attempt. Repeating the same result is accepted, since the agent cannot know whether its first report arrived; a different result for an attempt already finished is refused.
Spend a registration token to receive an agent identity and its long-lived token. The token is returned only here. Retrying with the same request key reports that the enrolment already completed.
Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will be called by the restored system with a one-time boot token, enrolling it as a new system. Until then a restore stops at awaiting_boot.
post.summary: Report that a restored system booted

parameters.description: Recovery ID injected into the rescue instance
parameters.name: recoveryId

post.description: Called by the agent of an instance booted into rescue mode for a restore. Presenting the job's claim token returns the restore plan and repository access. Retrying with the same request key returns the same response until the redelivery window closes.

parameters.description: Recovery ID injected into the rescue instance
parameters.name: recoveryId

post.description: Called by the rescue agent while it restores. The first report moves a claimed job to restoring. Reports carry an increasing sequence number; one older than the last recorded is accepted and ignored.

parameters.description: Recovery ID injected into the rescue instance
parameters.name: recoveryId

post.description: Called by the rescue agent when the restore ends. A succeeded restore waits for its boot to be confirmed; a failed one ends the job. Repeating the recorded result is accepted, since the agent cannot know whether its first report arrived; a different result is refused.

parameters.description: Recovery ID injected into the rescue instance
parameters.name: recoveryId

get.description: List enrolled agents, most recently enrolled first, with when each was last heard from. An agent is offline when it has not been heard from for two minutes.

post.description: Revoke an agent's token, which stops working on its next request. Repeating this is safe. The agent keeps its local credentials, so enrolling it again takes "aiha-agent reset" on the host and a new registration token.

get.description: List backups across all systems, newest first, including those that failed or have not run yet. A backup that failed before producing a set has no backup set ID.

parameters.description: Only backups in this job status
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Only backups requested at or after this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Only backups requested before this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: to

get.description: Return what became of a backup set. This is the framework's record of what the agent reported: whether the files are still in the repository is not known here, and sizes are per set because the framework does not read manifests.
get.summary: Get a backup by its set ID

delete.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Backup data never passes through the framework, so deleting a set needs a job an agent carries out, which does not exist.

get.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will list state changes in sequence order, so that a reader can resume from the last one it saw.

parameters.description: Only events after this sequence number
parameters.name: after

get.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will list HA groups with their state, verdict and reasons.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will register two systems, the volume replicated between them and the service running on it. Registering configures nothing: see setup.

get.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will return the group's state, the verdict with its reasons, and each node's health and replication status.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. A group in error stays there until an operator has dealt with the cause and says so here.
post.summary: Clear an HA group's error state

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will promote the standby of a group whose primary stopped answering. The framework never does this on its own judgement: the caller must confirm the primary is fenced, and accept any replication gap.
Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will discard what the old primary wrote after the switch and resynchronize it. This cannot be undone, so it only ever runs on explicit request.
post.summary: Rejoin a returned node to its HA group

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Nothing promotes automatically, so a rebooted primary comes back secondary with its service stopped. This will promote it again without changing roles.
post.summary: Resume an HA group's primary after a reboot

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will queue replication setup on the standby and then the primary, ending in the initial synchronization. Follow it by the group's state.

Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will demote the primary, and only once that is confirmed promote the standby. For a planned move while both nodes are healthy. Will be refused while another job runs on either node.
post.summary: Switch an HA group to its standby

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will stop and clean up replication on both nodes.

get.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will list the group's switches and recoveries, with who approved each and whether fencing was confirmed.
Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will list redundancy, switch, backup and restore work and incidents in one timeline (SFR-HA-07).
Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will list incidents by target, type and period.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will record an incident on behalf of the HA support agent.

get.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Will return an incident's events, diagnoses, alarms and actions.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Actions will refer to the switch or restore job they caused rather than copy its history.
Not implemented yet: answers 501.
Not implemented yet: answers 501. Diagnoses will accumulate rather than replace one another, so it stays visible which one an action was approved on.
Not implemented yet: answers 501.

get.description: List jobs, newest first. Restores have their own list at /restores: a rescue agent is not an enrolled system, so they are not in this queue.

parameters.description: Only jobs created at or after this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Only jobs created before this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: to

get.description: Return a job and the attempt carrying it out. LastSeenAt and LastProgressAt are separate on purpose: an agent that is seen but not progressing is alive and stuck, while one that is not seen has lost contact.

post.description: A job still queued is cancelled at once (200). A job an agent is running is only marked (202): the agent learns of it on its next report and has to confirm it stopped, and until then the job stays cancelling. Repeating a cancel is safe. A job that already ended any other way is refused.

202.description: Waiting for the agent to stop

get.description: Report whether the AI-HA framework has completed initialization and can accept requests.
get.summary: Check whether the framework is ready

get.description: List issued registration tokens and what is left of them. The tokens themselves are not stored and cannot be listed.

post.description: Issue a token that lets an agent enrol, with the settings the agent needs to reach this framework. It authorizes enrolment and nothing else. The token is returned only here and cannot be recovered: if an agent never receives its credentials, revoke the incomplete agent and issue a new one. An empty request issues a token good for one enrolment within 30 minutes.
Revoke a registration token so that it can enrol nothing further. Agents it already enrolled are unaffected. Repeating this is safe.

get.description: List the registered repositories, by name. Credentials are never returned.

post.description: Register an S3 repository (AWS or MinIO) that backups can write to. The credentials are stored encrypted, and an agent receives them only with a job it has claimed. The location cannot be changed afterwards: register a new repository for a new location. Whether the repository can be reached is not checked here.

get.description: Return a registered repository, without its credentials.

put.description: Replace a repository's credentials, keeping its ID and location, so jobs and backup sets that name it stay valid. The old credentials are not read, which also recovers a repository whose secret key was lost.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. A check from the framework says nothing about whether an agent inside a customer network can write there, so a real answer needs a job an agent carries out.
post.summary: Check that a repository can be reached

get.description: List restore jobs, newest first.

parameters.description: Only restores of this source system
parameters.name: systemId

parameters.description: Only restores of this backup set
parameters.name: backupSetId

parameters.description: Only restores requested at or after this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Only restores requested before this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: to

post.description: Register a restore job for a backup set and return at once: follow it at the address in the Location header. The set must be one a backup job reported as completed; that job says which system it captured and which repository holds it. Target instances are still created by hand, so the response carries, this once, what the instance's init script needs, including its claim token. "Completed" is what the agent reported: whether the files are still in the repository is found out by the rescue agent. Requests are not deduplicated yet: repeating one registers another job.

get.description: Return a restore's status, the step its rescue agent is on and how much of the backup files it has read. A status of awaiting_boot means the disk was restored; the restored system's boot has not been confirmed.

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. A rescue agent has no path to receive a cancel, and past formatting a stopped restore does not return the disk to its earlier state.

get.description: Return the generated OpenAPI (Swagger) document describing this API.
List the systems an agent has enrolled for, most recently enrolled first, with the state of the agent speaking for each. An online agent is reachable; that does not say its work is healthy.
Return one protected system and how current its inventory is. The inventory is absent until the agent first reports.

post.description: Queue a backup job for the system's agent and return at once: follow the job at the address in the Location header. With no devices the partitions are chosen from what the agent reported; a system whose report is missing or incomplete is refused, because a set chosen from it could leave out a filesystem the system needs, and only the restore would show it. Named devices are checked against the same report. If there is no report yet they are accepted unchecked, with a warning, and the agent checks them before it writes. Requests are not deduplicated yet: repeating one queues another job.
post.summary: Request a backup of a system

get.description: Return what the system's agent last reported. The framework cannot read a system itself, so this is always a past reading: check when it was collected before relying on it.
get.summary: Get what a system is made of

post.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Agents report on startup and periodically, and no job kind carries this request to them.
post.summary: Ask a system's agent to report its inventory again

put.description: Not implemented yet: answers 501. Targets are chosen per backup request, from the inventory or by name.
put.summary: Set what a system's backups capture

registrationTokenId.description:
RegistrationTokenID is the token that enrolled the agent, which finds an
agent that never received its enrolment response.

status.description: Status is online, offline or revoked.

collectedAt.description:
CollectedAt is when the agent read the system, which is not when the
framework heard about it. Backup targets chosen from a stale inventory
can name a partition that no longer exists.

complete.description:
Complete is false when the agent could not account for every filesystem
the system needs. Backup targets are not chosen automatically from an
inventory that says so.

incompleteReason.description: IncompleteReason explains Complete being false, in an operator's terms.

missing.description: Missing names the filesystems that were unaccounted for, e.g. "/boot/efi".

spec.description: Spec is what to do, passed through as the job was created.

claimRequestKey.description:
ClaimRequestKey scopes idempotency to this one request. A retry reuses
it; a stale request with a different key cannot join a newer attempt.
32 hexadecimal digits.

leaseToken.description:
LeaseToken proves this attempt is current. Every report carries it. It
is returned only here.

progressIntervalSeconds.description:
ProgressIntervalSeconds is how often to report, whether or not the work
has advanced. LeaseSeconds is how long a report buys. They are sent here
rather than compiled into the agent so that they can be tuned without
redeploying.

repository.description:
Repository is where the job writes, with the credentials to do so. It is
sent only in this response and stored nowhere with the job.

advanced.description:
Advanced says whether the work moved since the last report. A report
that only proves the agent is alive sets it false, which keeps an agent
that is up but stuck distinguishable from one that is gone.

processedBytes.description: ProcessedBytes is how much has been uploaded so far.

seq.description: Seq orders reports within an attempt. An older one is ignored.

cancelRequested.description:
CancelRequested tells the agent to stop. There is no inbound path to an
agent, so this is the only way a cancel can reach it.

detail.description: Detail is what the attempt produced, recorded as reported.

outcome.description: Outcome is completed, failed or cancelled.

hostname.description: Hostname and AgentVersion are recorded for display and diagnosis.

registrationKey.description:
RegistrationKey identifies this enrolment attempt. A retry reuses it so
that the framework recognises a repeat instead of enrolling a second
agent. 32 hexadecimal digits.

registrationToken.description:
RegistrationToken authorizes the enrolment. It is spent by a successful
registration and authorizes nothing else: it cannot receive work.

systemId.description:
SystemID is the machine this agent protects. The agent proposes it; what
makes the enrolment legitimate is the registration token, never this.

agentToken.description: AgentToken authenticates every later request, as a bearer token.

devices.description: Devices are the partitions the job will capture.

warnings.description:
Warnings are reasons to look twice that did not stop the request, such
as an inventory too old to trust.

items.description:
Items is how many backup files the set holds, and Manifest names the
file describing them in the repository.

processedBytes.description: ProcessedBytes is how much was uploaded, compressed.

setStatus.description:
SetStatus is the set's own status as the agent reported it, which can be
partial when some of its items failed.

compression.description: Compression names the codec, empty for the default.

devices.description:
Devices are the partitions to capture. Left out, they are chosen from
what the system's agent reported.

repositoryId.description: RepositoryID is the ID or name of the registered repository to write to.

certPin.description:
CertPin says the agent pins the certificate named by CertSHA256, for a
self-signed certificate. False means it verifies the certificate against
its CA bundle, and CertSHA256 is empty.

incidentId.description: IncidentID links the action to the incident it answers, if any.
IncidentID links the action to the incident it answers, if any.

state.description:
State is registered, configuring, syncing, protected, degraded,
failover_pending, switching or error. It governs what may be done next.

verdict.description:
Verdict is ok, attention or error, derived anew at each evaluation, and
Reasons explains it. It is not State: a broken replication link is a
verdict of error on a group that is degraded.

serviceAddress.description:
ServiceAddress is where clients reach the service. It is recorded so
that a completed switch can say what to repoint.

device.description:
Device is what the filesystem sits on, and BackingDisk the volume holding
the data on each node, as a stable by-id path.

name.description:
Name identifies the replication resource. Empty has the framework issue
one; set, it adopts a resource that already exists.

expectedGpus.description:
ExpectedGPUs is how many accelerators each node must see. Zero skips
the check.

kind.description: Kind is switchover, failover, resume or rejoin.

status.description:
Status is pending, running, completed or failed, and Phase the step it
is on.

candidate.description:
Candidate says this partition is included when backup targets are chosen
automatically. Selectable says it may be named by hand. They differ: a
partition can be selectable without being a candidate, while one that is
not selectable cannot be captured at all and is refused even when asked
for by name.

device.description:
Device is the canonical device path. It is resolved from the mount's
device number rather than copied from the mount table, whose source name
can be an alias ("/dev/root" on cloud images) that cannot be backed up.
It is empty when the path could not be resolved, which is why it is not
required: a partition that is present but unreadable reads very
differently from one that is absent.

fsSizeBytes.description:
FSSizeBytes and FSUsedBytes are the filesystem's size and usage, not the
device's. Null means the value could not be determined, which is not the
same as a filesystem that is empty.

reason.description: Reason explains a false in either flag, in an operator's terms.

complete.description:
Complete is false when the agent could not account for every filesystem
the system needs. Backup targets are then not chosen automatically.

stale.description: Stale says the reading is old enough that the system may have changed.

lastSeenAt.description:
LastSeenAt moves with every report and LastProgressAt only when the work
advanced, so an agent that is alive but stuck can be told from one that
is gone. LeaseExpiresAt is when the attempt loses its authority.

outcome.description:
Outcome is completed, failed, cancelled or unknown; unknown means the
agent stopped reporting, which is not a confirmed failure.

processedBytes.description:
ProcessedBytes is how much has been handled so far. TotalUnknown says
there is no total to set it against: show throughput and elapsed time
rather than a percentage.

result.description: Result is what the agent reported producing, recorded as reported.

attempt.description:
Attempt is the execution in progress or the last one. It is absent until
an agent claims the job, and in lists.

cancelRequested.description:
CancelRequested says a cancel was asked for. A running job only stops
once its agent confirms it.

spec.description: Spec is what the agent was asked to do. It holds no credentials.

status.description:
Status is queued, claimed, running, cancelling, completed, failed or
cancelled.

agentStatus.description:
AgentStatus is online, offline or revoked. Online says the agent is
reachable, not that the system's work is healthy: an agent can be alive
while its job is stuck.

AgentStatus is online, offline or revoked. Online says the agent is
reachable, not that the system's work is healthy: an agent can be alive
while its job is stuck.

status.description: Status is usable, used_up, expired or revoked.

maxUses.description: MaxUses is how many agents the token may enrol.

note.description: Note records what the token was issued for.

ttlSeconds.description: TTLSeconds is how long the token may be used to enrol, at most a week.

sessionToken.description:
SessionToken makes the credentials temporary. It is not renewed by the
framework: replace the credentials when it expires.

hasSessionToken.description:
HasSessionToken says whether the credentials include a session token,
which expires and is not renewed by the framework.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the URL of an S3-compatible service, empty for AWS.

sessionToken.description:
SessionToken makes the credentials temporary. It is not renewed by the
framework: replace the credentials when it expires.

verifier.description:
Verifier is who checks: "framework", or "agent:<systemId>" to learn
whether that agent can really write there. Only the second predicts
whether a backup will succeed.

claimExpiresAt.description: ClaimExpiresAt is when the rescue agent must have claimed the job by.

rescue.description:
Rescue is what a rescue instance needs to take the job on. Target
instances are still created by hand, so the caller has to carry these
into the instance's init script. It is returned only here.

claimToken.description:
ClaimToken is the one-time secret injected through the instance's init
script.

requestKey.description:
RequestKey identifies this agent's claim. Retries reuse it so that a
response lost in transit can be fetched again.

plan.description: Plan is passed through as registered; its schema is RestorePlan.

reportToken.description:
ReportToken authenticates this agent's progress and result reports for
the restore. A new one is issued on every claim response, redeliveries
included, and only the latest is accepted. It is a secret.

bootVerification.description:
BootVerification is pending while the restored system's boot waits to be
confirmed. Confirming it is not implemented yet, so it stays pending.

restoreOutcome.description:
RestoreOutcome is how the agent said the restore ended, kept apart from
Status because a restored disk is not yet a system that boots.

status.description: Status is awaiting_agent, claimed, restoring, awaiting_boot or failed.

item.description: Item is the backup file being restored, while extracting.

processedBytes.description:
ProcessedBytes is how much has been read from the repository. TotalUnknown
says TotalBytes is not known yet.

item.description: Item is the backup file being restored, while extracting.

phase.description: Phase is the step being carried out, e.g. "extracting".

processedBytes.description:
ProcessedBytes is how much of the backup files has been read from the
repository; TotalBytes is their combined size.

seq.description: Seq orders reports within a restore. An older one is ignored.

step.description: Step and TotalSteps place Phase in the sequence, e.g. 4 of 6.

backupSetId.description:
BackupSetID must be a set a backup job reported as completed. That job
says which system it captured and which repository holds it.

phase.description: Phase is the step the restore ended in.

code.description:
Code identifies a failure for programs to branch on; Message is for
people and may be reworded. The management API sets it on the failures
it answers itself; one turned away earlier, such as by the rate limiter,
has only a message and its HTTP status.

ageSeconds.description:
AgeSeconds is how long ago the agent read the system, by the framework's
clock.

complete.description:
Complete is false when the agent could not account for every filesystem
the system needs. Backup targets are then not chosen automatically.

report.description: Report is the inventory as the agent sent it.

stale.description: Stale says the reading is old enough that the system may have changed.

AdminToken.description: Management API token, as "Bearer <token>". It is the file named by AIHA_FRAMEWORK_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE.
AdminToken.name: Authorization

AgentToken.description: The agent's own token, as "Bearer <token>", issued at enrolment.
AgentToken.name: Authorization

RestoreReportToken.description: The rescue agent's report token, as "Bearer <token>", issued in the claim response.
RestoreReportToken.name: Authorization
